replies.What is your relationship with mathemati: I'd say math is a bit of a struggle for me personally. I prefer subjects like economics and computer science where creativity and logic blend better. Although I have a vocational diploma, numbers and formulas often feel detached from real-world application for me, making it something I approach cautiously rather than with enthusiasm during my self-employed work.
replies.Do you ever get anxious when thinking ab: Honestly, not really. My personality traits suggest I'm quite emotionally stable. While I might feel a mild frustration when things don't click, I don't experience intense anxiety. I prefer to focus on what I'm good at, like writing or coding, rather than stressing over abstract equations that don't align with my vocational background.
replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: Yes, actually. I've used AI tools to help understand concepts in computer science and economics. It was really helpful because it explained things in simple terms, which I appreciate. I didn't use it for complex proofs, but for general understanding, it was a great supplement to my vocational studies and helped bridge gaps in my knowledge efficiently.

replies.Briefly, how do you perform a Principal: First, standardize your data so each variable has a mean of zero. Calculate the correlation matrix to see relationships. Find the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of that matrix. Sort them by size. The eigenvectors become your principal components. No need to be anxious; it's just finding patterns in data linearly.
